item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Lula looks **somewhat closer to his 2024 program by year-end than at the start**, mainly because the government turned the agenda into budgeted plans, delivered visible welfare gains, reduced deforestation, and preserved democratic/constitutional continuity. The biggest caveat is that **macro credibility, some institutional discipline, and vulnerable-group protection remained incomplete**, so this is not a clean or fully durable advance.

**Accepted Claims**
- **PPA 2024-2027 turned Lula’s agenda into a monitored, budget-linked plan** | **Ministry of Planning and Budget / Planalto** | **2024-12-19 / 2024-06-18** | https://www.gov.br/planejamento/pt-br/assuntos/planejamento/plano-plurianual/paginas/paginas-ppa-2024-2027/ppa-2024-2027-english | The government translated Lula’s program into six priorities, 88 programs, and formal monitoring/evaluation tied to annual budgets. This is strong evidence that he ended 2024 with a more operationalized governing program than at the start. | **QIDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Novo PAC channeled large-scale spending into health, education, sanitation, water, and housing** | **Casa Civil / Ministry of Health / Ministry of Cities / Ministry of Social Development** | **2024-03-07, 2024-04-25, 2024-07-26, 2024-11-05, 2024-08-16** | https://www.gov.br/casacivil/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/2024/marco/novo-pac-selecoes-vai-investir-r-23-bilhoes-em-saude-educacao-esporte-e-cultura | Lula’s administration moved from programmatic promises to concrete delivery architecture: clinics, schools, creches, sanitation, water, and post-flood housing. That supports a stronger “closer to goal” reading on the social-policy side. | **QIDs:** 8B.10

- **Food insecurity and poverty fell sharply in 2024** | **Ministry of Social Development / Agência Gov** | **2024-12-23** | https://www.gov.br/mds/pt-br/noticias-e-conteudos/desenvolvimento-social/noticias-desenvolvimento-social/2024-o-ano-do-combate-a-fome-e-reducao-da-pobreza | The government reported 24.4 million people leaving severe food insecurity and poverty falling to its lowest level since 2012. Even with official-source caveats, this is one of the clearest signs Lula was moving closer to his redistributive program. | **QIDs:** 8B.10, 8B.1, 8B.4

- **Amazon deforestation fell to the lowest level in nine years** | **Brazil Ministry of Environment and Climate Change / INPE** | **2024-11-06** | https://www.gov.br/mma/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/taxa-de-desmatamento-na-amazonia-cai-30-6-e-25-7-no-cerrado | Official 2024 estimates showed Amazon deforestation down 30.6% from 2023 and Cerrado deforestation down 25.7%. That is strong evidence Lula made measurable progress on a signature ideological and international-priority agenda. | **QIDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Lula expanded Brazil’s climate and regulatory machinery** | **Brazil Ministry of Environment and Climate Change / MDIC / Planalto** | **2024-09-10, 2024-08-21, 2024-06-18** | https://www.gov.br/mma/pt-br/lula-anuncia-criacao-de-autoridade-climatica | The Climate Authority, the “Regula Melhor” framework, and PPA governance reforms point to a more institutionalized state capacity than at the start of the year. This supports an end-of-year judgment that his program became more durable and administratively real. | **QIDs:** 8B.10, 5B.7

- **Brazil kept a peace-oriented and disarmament-oriented international posture** | **Planalto / Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Reuters via UOL** | **2024-01-08, 2024-05-23, 2024-09-22, 2024-09-24, 2024-10-25** | https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_Ato2023-2026/2024/Decreto/D12237.htm | Lula pursued Ukraine/Gaza diplomacy, supported ceasefire language, created a permanent disarmament delegation, and used UN/G20 speeches to argue for dialogue over militarization. That means Brazil’s international-influence program advanced, even if imperfectly. | **QIDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Municipal opposition wins were tolerated, not rolled back** | **Reuters via UOL / Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-10-27** | https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/10/27/partidos-de-centro-e-da-direita-consolidam-vitoria-no-2-turno-das-eleicoes-municipais.amp.htm | Opposition and center-right forces won major municipal races, including setbacks for Lula’s camp, and the reporting shows no retaliation or non-acceptance. That supports a “closer to the democratic/contestable end of the program” reading. | **QIDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Lula refused to endorse Venezuela’s claimed victory without proof** | **Reuters via UOL** | **2024-08-30** | https://economia.uol.com.br/noticias/reuters/2024/08/30/lula-reafirma-que-nao-aceita-vitoria-de-maduro-sem-provas.htm | Lula backed publication of vote records, possible new elections, and observers. This supports a claim that he favored procedural legitimacy and evidence-based contestation, not personalist alignment. | **QIDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Fiscal credibility improved somewhat, but only under pressure** | **Reuters via Investing.com / Reuters via UOL** | **2024-07-03, 2024-09-20, 2024-12-21** | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/brazils-lula-says-government-is-committed-to-fiscal-responsibility-3507587 | Lula approved spending cuts and the government later cut its deficit forecast and pushed a fiscal package through Congress. This is real movement toward the stated macro program, but it was reactive and did not fully resolve credibility concerns. | **QIDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Central-bank autonomy and fiscal credibility remained a major caveat** | **Reuters via UOL / Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-07-01, 2024-09-18, 2024-11-18** | https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/07/01/lula-critica-bc-autonomo-e-diz-que-autoridade-monetaria-nao-atende-populacao.htm | Lula publicly pressured the Central Bank, Reuters reported creative accounting around fiscal targets, and markets still worried about credibility. This is the strongest evidence that Lula was not clearly closer to his program on the macro/technocratic front by year-end. | **QIDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Strategic-firm steering and coalition protection were still unresolved** | **Reuters via UOL** | **2024-03-18, 2024-03-20, 2024-06-12, 2024-06-13** | https://economia.uol.com.br/noticias/reuters/2024/03/18/ministerio-publico-do-tcu-pede-investigacao-de-possivel-interferencia-do-governo-na-petrobras.htm | Petrobras dividend pressure and the decision not to immediately remove an indicted minister are the clearest signs that discretionary steering and patronage still competed with the programmatic, rules-based project. | **QIDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Yanomami and police-violence problems were improved but not solved** | **Reuters via UOL / Human Rights Watch** | **2024-01-26, 2024-03-15, 2025-01-01 covering 2024** | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/15/brazil-comply-rulings-police-violence | Lula’s state expanded operations and monitoring, but Yanomami invasion, malnutrition, violence, and police abuse persisted. That means the program advanced in intent and machinery, but the end-state was still far from fully achieved in practice. | **QIDs:** 8B.10, 3B.1, 8B.9

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a single source that directly measures “distance to Lula’s program” from January to December 2024. The judgment here is inferred from a combination of program translation, outcome changes, and residual constraints.
- The balance of evidence is enough to say **“closer than at the start, but unevenly and not durably across all fronts.”**
